per_plume.source_hint: Kilauea summit / S Hawaii Island; SW offshore haze
evidence: Plume is diffuse pale blue-gray translucent veil over dark ocean SW of Hawaii Island, distinct from bright white cumulus/cirrus; mask is 100% oceanic with no land spill, indicating reliable offshore haze mask rather than island-swamping cloud artifact. [E4]
Kilauea is WATCH/ORANGE with strong glow and flames continuing and Halema`uma`u seismicity (erupting unknown), while Mauna Loa is NORMAL/GREEN not erupting, favoring Kilauea as vog source. [E2]
FIRMS shows 122 volcanic-thermal pixels at Kilauea summit and zero fire clusters in plume box, confirming active Kilauea heat/degassing and no wildfire smoke source. [E6]

Wind at centroid is from 123 deg at 21.1 km/h (blowing toward ~303 deg WNW); with this wind the plume upwind SE end lies ~90.9 km from Kilauea and 109.0 km from Mauna Loa, with 289-km WNW-ESE axis consistent with trade-wind transport from island to offshore SW. [E1, E7]

Measured 3-h centroid drift is toward 125 deg at 7.5 km/h (R2 0.76), ~178 deg opposite wind-implied transport toward ~303 deg, and inferred NW source end lies >200 km from both summits offshore; this disagreement contradicts simple wind drift and lowers confidence. [E5, E1]

classify.caveats: Heavy white cloud over Hawaii Island partly obscures vent region; 3-h tracked drift opposes ERA5 wind, possibly from cloud-deck contamination or local flow; no fires and active Kilauea thermal support vog despite motion mismatch.

kilauea.activity_summary: No overflows or spattering at north or south vents over the past day; strong glow and flames continue. No reactivation of intrusion emplaced two nights ago. Earthquake activity continues underneath Halemaʻumaʻu.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in September compared to August, and minor inflation continues. Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 53 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the September reporting period, after 87 in August. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.
